Lucy Beaumont's point about what is legal vs what people find uncomfortable is really important on this front. I am not sure we should rush to legislate on age gaps but there's clearly a question about gauging consent in circumstances where power isn't equally held
Same power/age dynamics, same incentives to just act like everything is ok and say nothing
Obviously the independent complaints and grievance scheme (ICGS) has been set up to address this but it only goes so far
Many parallels with Westminster of course, where staff spend long hours in small offices with their employer. No central HR function= limited options if something happens

In 1996, a man was killed in Boston’s Chinatown. His identity remained publicly unknown for decades. Bellingcat spent over a year investigating to find his name and piece together his story with public records. TunnelVision filmed with our team as the investigation unfolded. youtu.be/oMhHsAvqVGs?...
